field_checks.summary: The final database layer has 5 record audits, with 2 unresolved fallback candidates and 3 sequence_modified_not_normalized candidates; no source_verified authoritative DBAASP/APD6/DRAMP rows are present. Fallback release boundary is preserved, but the current strict acceptance artifact reports 210 hard recursive_non_source_locator_reference findings in worker-4 database artifacts and both database final mirrors, so database provenance is not publication-grade.

Core common paper-final and packet-final artifacts are byte-identical, packet mechanism_evidence.json equals mechanism_ontology_record.json, and review_report counts match live final counts: 49 activity, 2 toxicity, 5 database audits, 5 mechanism claims. Exact file sets differ because papers/final has materials_manifest.json while packets/final has mechanism_evidence.json as an alias.

Mechanism ontology keeps evidence classes separated: one direct SEM/TEM/microscopy morphology claim, two phenotype-supported claims for MIC/growth and biofilm, one inferred design/structure-function claim, and one unknown-or-not-tested negative claim. No computational-only or inferred charge/structure language is promoted to direct mechanism.

Paper identity is correct for RSC Advances 2025, DOI 10.1039/d5ra02745d, PMID 40510052, title matching PMC12160004. Source entities A3, D-A3, A3-C4, A3-C5, and A3-C6 are linked to source synthesis/modification passages, and no object with both plain one-letter sequence and sequence_length was found. Caution remains because authoritative linked database rows are absent and source_verified database count is zero.

Locator presence is not enough: final activity normalization asserts direct uM units for 49 MIC rows whose primary source units are μg ml−1 or μg mL−1. Database citation_traceability source_locators also contain packet/database artifact paths, which the current strict acceptance audit flags as recursive non-source locators. Sequence-length checks found zero applicable objects and zero mismatches.

Fallback rows remain excluded from authoritative DBAASP ingest, but recursive authority boundary is not false: the strict acceptance artifact reports 210 hard recursive_non_source_locator_reference findings across database work, analysis, and both database final mirrors. Review_report still says publication_grade true and rework_targets 0, so the hard findings are unreconciled.

Final review preserves cautions for absent authoritative DBAASP rows, fallback-machine boundary, modified/not-normalized A3-C4/A3-C5/A3-C6 identities, and direct-imaging mechanism limitation. These cautions are valid but insufficient to clear the independent hard failures in activity units/toxicity coverage and recursive database locators.

All staged source surfaces are readable. The paper has one staged supplementary PDF, RA-015-D5RA02745D-s001.pdf; it is 17 pages, direct PDF text and OCR text have 17 records, XML supplementary media hrefs resolve to the staged PDF, and no extraction errors or live material gaps were found.

Final toxicity coverage is incomplete and partly conflated. The source hemolysis result covers A3 plus four derived peptides across 0.9-500 μg mL−1 and says derived peptides did not exceed 2.5%, but final toxicity contains only two A3 records, including an A3 2.5% row not supported as A3-specific. Zebrafish in vivo toxicity from xml:p:26/xml:p:40/xml:fig:11 is not represented as row-level toxicity/selectivity evidence or explicitly excluded.
